name: Melanotan II
summary: Synthetic melanocortin agonist that darkens skin by cranking melanin production. Also hits arousal and appetite.
note: Unapproved, gray-market, FDA-flagged safety concerns. Not the same thing as prescription afamelanotide.

name: Afamelanotide
summary: MC1R agonist that boosts eumelanin and photoprotection.
note: Strong evidence only for its approved light-sensitivity condition — it is not a cosmetic tan drug.

name: Dihydroxyacetone
summary: The active in every self-tanner: stains the outer skin layer brown. The only proven-safe tan in a bottle.

name: Canthaxanthin
summary: Carotenoid "tanning pill" that tints skin orange-brown at high doses.
note: Linked to crystal deposits in the retina. Unsafe strategy.

name: Beta-carotene
summary: Gives skin a warmer, golden tone with sustained daily intake.

name: Lycopene
summary: Tomato carotenoid with antioxidant and mild photoprotective effects.

name: Astaxanthin
summary: Carotenoid studied for UV damage, skin moisture, and elasticity.

name: Polypodium leucotomos
summary: Fern extract that blunts some UV-induced skin reactions.

name: Glutathione
summary: Antioxidant heavily marketed for skin lightening; visible results are inconsistent.

name: L-Cysteine
summary: Antioxidant precursor tied to melanin pathways; weak lightening evidence.

name: Teriparatide
summary: Anabolic bone drug that increases bone formation.
note: For osteoporosis — not cosmetic jaw enhancement.

name: Romosozumab
summary: Sclerostin-blocking antibody that builds bone and slows resorption.
note: Osteoporosis drug. Will not give you cheekbones.

name: Vitamin K2
summary: Cofactor for bone-mineralization proteins. Supplement trial data mixed.

name: Calcium
summary: Necessary for bone mineralization.
note: Strong only when dietary intake is inadequate.

name: Magnesium
summary: Required for normal skeletal and neuromuscular physiology.

name: Boron
summary: Trace element studied for mineral and hormone metabolism.

name: Caffeine (topical)
summary: Constricts vessels for a temporary under-eye depuff.

name: Hesperidin
summary: Vein-supporting flavonoid used for venous and microvascular issues.

name: Dandelion extract
summary: Marketed herbal diuretic. Weak evidence.

name: Potassium
summary: Electrolyte balance — fix the diet (and sodium) before buying pills.

name: Furosemide
summary: Powerful medical loop diuretic.
note: Strong medically — dangerous and pointless as a cosmetic face-slimming trick.
